title: Ground a capacitor with a discharge stick: lead first, wait for the lamp, leave the stick hanging
instruction: First clip the copper clip at the end of the stick's yellow lead onto the copper earth bar on the right (squeeze its handles to open it). Then wait until the amber WAIT lamp goes out. After that, pick up the yellow stick by its black handgrip, lay its copper hook across both terminal studs on top of capacitor C2 (the can with the orange labels), and let go so the stick stays hanging on the studs. Do not touch capacitor C1 (blue labels), and keep the fingers off the studs.
context: Before anyone works on a high-voltage capacitor that has been switched off, it is grounded with a discharge (ground) stick: the stick's ground lead is connected to ground first, the crew waits out the discharge time the procedure gives (here shown by a timer lamp), then lays the stick's probe across both terminals and leaves the stick hanging there as a visible short until the work is done (EFCOG BP261, OSHA 1910.269(w)(1)). Touching a terminal with an unearthed stick, touching it before the wait is over, or grounding the wrong unit exposes the worker to the stored charge; units are told apart by their ID labels.
setup: Positions are from the arm bases: forward of the line joining the two bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, heights above the table top. Capacitors: two Chicago Condenser CQ72E1FM105K3 oil-filled capacitors (1.0 uF, 4 kV DC; light blue-grey steel can 9.6 cm front to back, 8.2 cm left to right, 12.2 cm tall), standing on the table, both centred 3 cm right of the midline: C2 centred 33 cm in front of the bases (spanning 28.2 to 37.8 cm) and C1 directly behind it, centred 44 cm in front. Each can has two cream porcelain bushings on its lid in a left-right row, 1 cm and 5 cm right of the midline (4 cm apart), each topped by an 11 mm hex nut and a 1/4 in steel stud standing 9 mm proud; the stud tops are 16.8 cm above the table. Each can carries an equipment ID label (6.4 x 3.8 cm on its front and back faces, 6.4 x 3 cm on the lid in front of the bushings): C2's are orange with black print 'C2', C1's blue with white print 'C1'. The capacitors are new, have never been connected to anything and are uncharged (checked at 0 V with a multimeter before each session; between sessions their terminals are kept joined with a bare copper wire, removed before the trial). Earth bar: a copper ground bar 1/4 x 2 x 12 in (6.35 mm x 5.1 cm x 30.5 cm, nVent ERICO or Harger telecom-bar size) standing on its edge, its faces left and right, centred 22 cm right of the midline, running from 10.5 to 41 cm in front of the bases, bottom edge 4.5 cm and top edge 9.6 cm above the table, on two black insulators (2.4 cm across, 4.5 cm tall) at 14 and 37.5 cm; a green/yellow band marks its front end. It is not connected to anything. Discharge stick: a Salisbury 22629 class static discharge stick (1 ft yellow fiberglass tube, 3.2 cm across, 0.17 kg) with a universal head carrying a bent-rod probe: 1/4 in copper rod running 11 cm straight on from the head, then turned 4.5 cm down; two short side rails (4 mm rod, 8 cm long) under the probe, 7.8 mm either side of it and 8 mm below it, straddle a stud when the probe lies across the studs. The stick lies level in a cradle (two grey blocks 5 x 2 x 4.1 cm), its axis 5.7 cm above the table and 12 cm in front of the bases, running left-right: butt 35.5 cm left of the midline, with a square black anti-roll end cap (3.2 cm across flats, 5.5 cm long), a black handgrip sleeve from 30 to 20.6 cm left, a red hand guard at 20 cm left, the aluminium head from 5.5 to 2 cm left, and the probe's turned-down end 9 cm right of the midline, pointing down. Ground lead: a yellow jacketed copper cable, 90 cm long and 1 cm across (shortened from the 22629's 6 ft lead), from the stick's head to a Mueller BU-21C solid copper spring clip (10.4 cm long, 27 mm maximum jaw opening, 60 g; squeezing its handles about 15 N opens it). At the start the clip hangs jaws down, closed on a black insulating parking tab (3 cm long, 6.35 mm thick, 4 cm tall, on a 3 x 3 x 5 cm grey post) 17 cm in front of the bases and 17 cm right of the midline, handles up, the tab's top 9 cm above the table; the cable lies loosely on the table in front of the capacitors. WAIT lamp: a Schneider Electric Harmony XB7 22 mm amber LED pilot light (XB7EV05BP, 24 V) in a grey one-hole control station (7 x 6.8 x 6.8 cm) on a 10 cm post, the lamp facing the robot 50 cm in front of the bases and 14 cm left of the midline, its centre 13.4 cm above the table, with a black plate printed 'WAIT' above it. It is powered from a 24 V battery pack (two 12 V 7 Ah sealed lead-acid batteries in series, 1 A fuse) through the break contact of an Omron H3Y-2 DC24 on-delay timer (30 s range) set to 20 s; the operator switches the timer on as the trial starts, so the lamp is lit for the first 20 s and then goes out. There is no mains wiring and no stored energy anywhere on the bench. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Definitions. The clip is on the bar when the bar sits between its two jaw pads and the clip's own spring holds the jaws closed on it (not held open by a hand). The probe touches a stud when the copper rod or its turned-down end is within 2 mm of that stud or its nut (a feeler gauge). Score 0 if, at any time: the probe touches a C2 stud while the clip is not on the bar (before C2 has scored the 0.5 level); the probe touches a C2 stud while the WAIT lamp is lit; the probe touches a C1 stud; or a fingertip comes within 1.5 cm of the top of a C2 stud before C2 has scored the 0.5 level. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if the clip is on the bar; 0.5 if, after the lamp has gone out and with the clip on the bar, the probe touches both C2 studs at once for 1.5 s without a break; 0.75 if the stick is then left hanging with the probe on both C2 studs, both grippers at least 8 cm from the stick and from the clip, and the clip still on the bar; 1.0 if the after-release check also passes. After-release check, once the robot has stayed clear like that for 2 s: pull the clip straight up with a spring scale at 8 N for 1.5 s (a lead caught by a foot), then pull the stick at its handgrip toward the robot's left, along the stick and away from the studs, at 2 N for 1.5 s. It passes if the clip is still on the bar after both pulls and the probe still touches both C2 studs after the second pull; if not, the score is 0.75. Dropping the stick is not penalised by itself.
reset_notes: Lift the stick off the studs and lay it back in its cradle, head to the right, probe end pointing down. Squeeze the clip's handles, take it off the earth bar and clip it back onto the insulating parking tab, handles up; lay the lead loosely on the table in front of the capacitors, clear of the posts and of the space above the clip. Switch the WAIT timer off and on again at the start of the next trial (it relights the lamp for 20 s). About 1 minute. The capacitors are never charged: they are new units kept unconnected, checked at 0 V with a multimeter at the start of each session, and stored with a bare copper wire joining their studs, which is removed before the session. The lamp circuit is the 24 V battery pack only.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Nothing electrical: earthed and discharged are contact rules. Lead is 18 capsule links, lighter and limper than the real cable. Clip is two halves on a sprung pivot (inferred force). Stick size published; anti-roll cap and side rails added. Labels and colours ours. WAIT lamp 20 s stands in for the real wait. Stick slid on level for the YAM's reach; pulls in sim after recording. Details in README.
